title: React motion studio
summary: Build scoped, sequenced React animations with lifecycle cleanup.

stages.title: Establish animation primitives
stages.task: Choose targets and tweens; document reduced-motion alternatives.

stages.title: Compose the sequence
stages.task: Create named labels and intentional timing from the approved motion brief.

stages.title: Integrate and verify cleanup
stages.task: Use scoped refs and useGSAP; check rerenders, unmount and reduced motion.

requirements: React, gsap and @gsap/react. Runtime library terms are separate from skill MIT licenses.
conflicts: Core examples do not override React lifecycle guidance. Use gsap-react cleanup in React. ScrollTrigger and other plugins are outside this pack.
compatibility: Static workflow proposal; no end-to-end Codex runtime test.

title: Industrial interface + motion
summary: Apply a deliberate monochrome identity, then add restrained interaction.

stages.title: Set the visual system
stages.task: Apply Nothing-inspired styling only when explicitly requested; record tokens and readable contrast.

stages.title: Add functional motion
stages.task: Animate only interactions justified by the brief; preserve reduced-motion behavior.

requirements: A web project and GSAP runtime. Optional external fonts need separate setup.
conflicts: Keep nothing-design as the visual owner; GSAP only owns animation. Codex compatibility of nothing-design is unknown. Do not let motion change the typography or layout.
compatibility: Static workflow proposal; no end-to-end Codex runtime test.

title: Article to presentation
summary: Create an editorial web article and adapt its evidence into a presentation.

stages.title: Produce the source article
stages.task: Write the approved article with traceable claims and export a stable content outline.

stages.title: Adapt to presentation scenes
stages.task: Use that outline as input; review story, scene outline and rendered presentation at separate checkpoints.

requirements: Vite, React and TypeScript for generated projects. Optional TTS requires separate services; source skills are Chinese.
conflicts: Pass an article/outline between stages, not conflicting project scaffolds. Use separate output directories. Adapt upstream agent/reviewer instructions to your host; do not assume subagents or voice services exist.
compatibility: Static workflow proposal; no end-to-end Codex runtime test.

title: Evidence to editorial report
summary: Evaluate provided evidence before turning it into a readable web report.

stages.title: Appraise supplied evidence
stages.task: Create a source/claim/limitation table from user-provided papers; core appraisal only, no optional schematic service.

stages.title: Publish the bounded conclusions
stages.task: Use the approved evidence table to build an editorial article; keep uncertainty, references and missing evidence visible.

requirements: User-provided sources; frontend tooling for article output. No database retrieval, paid figures or TTS is included.
conflicts: Critical-thinking owns claim strength; article design must not inflate certainty. Optional sibling skills are excluded. This is not a clinical recommendation workflow.
compatibility: Static workflow proposal; no end-to-end Codex runtime test.

title: React architecture review
summary: Plan composable components, then review rendering performance.

stages.title: Define component boundaries
stages.task: Replace boolean-heavy APIs using compound components and explicit state ownership.

stages.title: Audit performance
stages.task: Review the resulting components for rendering and loading problems; retain approved public APIs.

requirements: React project. Install each skill using its pinned setup instructions.
conflicts: Architecture owns the component contract; performance changes must preserve it. Recipe only: complete redistributable license evidence for every member is not yet captured.
compatibility: Static workflow proposal; no end-to-end Codex runtime test.

title: Scholarly research pipeline
summary: Plan a search, gather evidence, then critically appraise the findings.

stages.title: Define the review protocol
stages.task: Define databases, date range, inclusion/exclusion and screening log before searching.

stages.title: Collect a bounded evidence packet
stages.task: Collect source excerpts with explicit provider consent; do not confuse retrieval with claim verification.

stages.title: Appraise claims
stages.task: Evaluate the included full texts and document bias, uncertainties and applicability.

requirements: Upstream installation, Python 3.10+, network and Parallel authentication; optional OpenRouter/PDF tooling.
conflicts: Literature-review owns the protocol. Research-lookup is a retrieval assistant, not a systematic-review engine. No claim of exhaustive coverage. Recipe only because service and sibling dependencies need upstream setup.
compatibility: Static workflow proposal; no end-to-end Codex runtime test.
